As we head into New York Climate Week alongside UNGA80, the energy access challenge remains urgent: 2.1 billion people still lack clean cooking and 666 million live without electricity.
 
Closing these gaps isn’t just about finance and infrastructure - it’s also about having the right data to make smarter decisions.
 
That is why, in partnership with IBM and Stony Brook University, UNDP has co-developed two open, AI-driven tools now available on GeoHub: https://lnkd.in/epWZQYhA

⚡ Electricity Access Forecasting Model - projecting access to 2030 across 100+ countries to help identify underserved areas.
⚡ Clean Energy Equity Index - assessing equity across 53 African countries to guide just, inclusive energy transitions.
 
Already informing UNDP projects expected to benefit 600,000+ people, these tools demonstrate how AI and open data can transform energy planning - moving us from static surveys to predictive, real-time insights.
 
Ultimately, closing energy access gaps isn’t just about building infrastructure or mobilizing finance. It’s about ensuring that every clean energy investment is guided by the right data - making progress toward SDG7 more targeted, equitable and achievable.
